skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2, before substantive questions, said counsel represents the Committee and company only, not the witness, and cannot give legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explained privilege belongs to the company, which decides waiver and may disclose to the government without the witness's consent.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explained how the interview would run, asked for complete answers, flagged speculation and recollection versus reconstruction, and noted the right to counsel.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asked whether the witness understood and had questions; T4 had the witness restate who was represented and who controls privilege.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T374 covered keeping documents and notes, confidentiality, not discussing with witnesses, possible follow-up, and asked for anything to add.

moments.text: We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
Explained how the interview would proceed, ground rules on speculation and recollection, and the right to consult counsel.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations at T16, T44, T80 and T310 let the witness walk through LJM1, Chewco, LJM2 controls and the 2001 payment.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Generally moves from role and process to specific transactions, but revisits earlier points (T334, T350) and jumps between topics in places.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are clear, but T210 combines a leading premise with a compound question about what the Board should have known.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Tone stays neutral and controlled even when confronting contradictions, e.g. T148 and T306, with polite framing throughout.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Pressed for estimates (T114-T118) and pursued the Foundation after T123, but did not use the approval sheet when the witness said it would show dates (T101).

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how Chewco came to be formed in 1997.
Leading compound question about whether the Board should have known LJM2 returns were several times what it had been told.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Challenged key inconsistencies (T19-T23, T29-T31 against T142-T151, T213-T219, T306-T309), but let T289 and T361 denials pass unchallenged.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Established who, what, when and how for Southampton, Chewco and the payment, but did not pin down the LLC bonus mechanism raised at T15.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Asked for recollection before showing minutes (T62-T70), Southampton and the note, but did not show the Raptor I approval sheet despite the witness pointing to it.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Separated firsthand from secondhand knowledge on Skilling's Board report (T56-T57), Chewco, McMahon's concerns (T229-T237) and the note (T305-T309).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: Asked who else to speak with and identified Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, McMahon, Lay, Skilling, Mintz and Andersen (T352-T359).

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: Asked for deal files, Foundation statements, investor reports, minutes and personal notes and emails, and asked where those are kept (T368-T373).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Asked how certain the witness was of the $4.5M figure, the $229M figure and the timing of the counsel call (T144, T216-T223, T318).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Followed up nearly all material leads, but the key lead about the LLC paying LJM bonuses (T15) was never pursued, capping this at 3.

moments.text: Earlier you said you told the Board you would not receive any current or future value from the Enron stock in LJM. Is that still your recollection?
How certain are you of that figure?
What's your best estimate?
Witness conceded that Skilling telling the Board was only his understanding, not personal knowledge.
Do you have any personal files, notes, or emails about LJM, Chewco, or Southampton?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Authenticated the Southampton agreement, minutes, investor report and note (T70-T74, T128-T135, T194-T199, T300-T303), but did not use the Raptor I approval sheet.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Asked for recollection before each document (T62-T69, T126-T127, T192-T193, T254-T255, T296-T299) and only then showed it.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Described documents accurately, quoting 'was not at risk' and 'tremendous utilization' and citing the $25,000 contribution and the 17.95 versus 51 percent figures correctly.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Mostly asked the witness to explain, but T210 is leading and T306 presents the contradiction sharply before the witness had a chance to explain.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: Gave the witness room to explain after each document, e.g. T150-T151, T252-T253, T262-T265 and T306-T307, before moving on.

moments.text: I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
I'm not suggesting you wrote it.
Our information is that Talon hadn't yet done any derivatives with Enron. Help me understand how those fit together.
Put the Andy note's $10.5M reference against the witness's earlier account and asked him to reconcile them.

missed_opportunities: T15: Key lead: Kopper's LLC paid Global Finance staff LJM bonuses outside Enron payroll. Never followed up. Ask: “Which LLC did Michael Kopper set up to pay those bonuses, who received payments from it, how much, and where are the records?”

T101: Witness said the Raptor I approval sheet would show the signing dates, but the sheet was never shown to refresh memory on timing and signatures. Ask: “Before we look at the Raptor I approval sheet, what dates and signatures do you remember, and what do those dates show?”
